Definition: a sending out, i.e. (abstractly) presentation (favorable), or seizure (unfavorable); also (concretely) a place of dismissal, or a business to be discharged
BiblicalUsage: The word is a sending out, a putting forth of the hand, and it covers both work and gifts. God blesses all that the hand is put to, and the Jews of the villages made Purim a day of sending portions one to another.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the open hand is blessed twice: God blesses the work of the hand, and the hand that sends portions to a neighbour is blessed again.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
